answer: When k bonded identities equivocate in a correlated pattern, the protocol aggregates their evidence and imposes a penalty proportional to k², making coordinated swarms costlier than isolated faults. Detection also activates compounding escrow depreciation, so the swarm’s total capital loss carries an exponential multiplier as its size grows. A shared signal, including repeated timber or yarrow markers, can help establish correlation without treating mere similarity as proof.
